title: Quant canary oscillation, traffic-shift flip and mitigation playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: A production regression was observed where a recent automated canary/traffic-shift for a quantized model alternated between the int8 variant and the float32 baseline, producing a sustained crashloop and transient accuracy drift for a subset of customer requests. This ticket captures the post-incident analysis, immediate mitigations, and a prioritized action plan to prevent recurrence and harden rollouts of quantized artifacts.

Context: The rollout system performs a phased traffic shift when a new quantized model build passes canary telemetry. During a 2025-02-10 rollout we observed repeated rollbacks and retries driven by flapping canary pass/fail signals. The flapping caused rapid kernel-selection churn on serving nodes leading to elevated OOMs and a 15-minute outage window for affected backends.
impact_summary: Approx. 13 backend instances experienced crash loops over a 17-minute window; ~1200 requests received degraded responses with higher perplexity and several customers reported regressions in classification thresholds. No data exfiltration. Incident surfaced by automated SLO alerts and customer support tickets. Estimated revenue-impact window: 00:15-00:32 UTC on 2025-02-10.
timeline: 2025-02-10T00:14Z - Canary rollout started: quantized-int8 model variant promoted to 5% traffic
2025-02-10T00:18Z - Alerts triggered: anomaly in per-token latency and memory; autoscaler attempted to rehome pods
2025-02-10T00:21Z - Canary evaluator reported accuracy regression exceeding threshold for recent prompt sample set
2025-02-10T00:23Z - Rollout controller initiated automatic rollback to float32 baseline; several warm caches invalidated
2025-02-10T00:26Z - Observed flip: rolled forward again due to transient telemetry gap in aggregator (missing batch normalization ratio), causing kernel selection mismatch
2025-02-10T00:31Z - Manual mitigation: ops pinned affected route to float32 variant and disabled auto-rollouts for quantized builds (hotfix policy)
2025-02-10T00:40Z - Crashloops subsided after rehoming and restart; full traffic restored by 00:45Z
2025-02-11T10:00Z - Incident review kickoff; initial hypotheses collected
2025-02-13T15:00Z - Reproduction in staging: synthetic workload reproduced kernel selection churn when batch-size = 4 and packed-weight-endian mismatch present

2025-02-18T09:30Z - Root cause confirmed: telemetry aggregator mis-aggregated per-batch token metrics for quantized backends during partial KV cache hits, causing canary evaluator to oscillate between pass/fail states
root_cause: A combination of three factors: (1) the telemetry aggregator computed normalized perplexity by dividing by an unstable per-batch token count when KV cache hits were partial, producing noisy accuracy signals for quantized backends; (2) the rollout controller used a short evaluation window (30s) and aggressive thresholding which amplified noise into flapping decisions; (3) a subtle kernel-selection race in the runtime manifested for specific batch sizes (4) when packed-weight endian assumptions differed across build environments, causing intermittent op fallback and increased memory churn. Together these produced oscillation that cascaded to crash loops during traffic shifts.
mitigations: Hotfix: pin routes to float32 variant for affected customers and disable auto-rollouts for new quantized builds until safeguards are in place (completed 2025-02-10)
Increase canary evaluation window from 30s to 5m for quantized model rollouts (temporary config change applied 2025-02-11)
Throttle rollout control plane to require stable telemetry for at least 3 consecutive windows before promoting (applied 2025-02-12)
Add runtime guard: prefer deterministic kernel selection path when packed-weight endian mismatch is detected (deployed as patch on staging 2025-02-17)
Restore auto-rollouts after canary safeguards validated (planned for 2025-02-25)
Alerting: new SLI on canary oscillation rate + noise amplification metric (added 2025-02-13)
Customer comms: support ops notified impacted accounts and provided a summary of mitigation actions (completed)
Rollback policy updated to prefer graceful degradation (route diversion) over immediate full rollback in case of noisy telemetry (design PR #4682)
action_items: Implement stable token-normalization in the telemetry aggregator: compute moving-average token counts and expose per-variant breakdowns (owner: telemetry team, estimate: 5)
Extend canary evaluator UI to show raw per-batch vectors + smoothing overlays so reviewers can detect noise vs signal (owner: console-ux, estimate: 3)
Add deterministic fallback kernel path and unit tests for packed-weight endian permutations across build environments (owner: runtime team, estimate: 8)
Create an end-to-end staging test that reproduces partial KV cache hit patterns at different batch sizes to catch kernel-selection races (owner: infra, estimate: 5)
Hard gate: block quantized builds from auto-rollout unless they pass a dedicated quant-canary suite that includes adversarial prompt sets (owner: release-engineering, estimate: 3)
Improve observability: add metric for canary flapping frequency and require <1 flap per 24h for auto-approve (owner: SRE, estimate: 2)
Post-incident blameless retro and documentation: publish full timeline + learnings to confluence and run workshop with SDK/runtime teams (owner: incident-review, estimate: 2)
Update runbook: include explicit steps to pin routes, extend windows, and perform graceful traffic diversion for quantized rollouts (owner: SRE, estimate: 1)
Backfill failing unit/regression tests uncovered during analysis into nightly CI (owner: runtime, estimate: 4)
decisions: Increase default canary window for quantized builds to 5 minutes (decided 2025-02-11)
Introduce a hard gating step in release pipeline for quantized artifacts requiring a dedicated quant-canary test suite (decided 2025-02-13)
Prefer route diversion to baseline variant over immediate rollback when telemetry shows high noise (decided 2025-02-14)
Require packed-weight format validation in the CI artifact checker to avoid endian mismatches across build farms (decided 2025-02-16)
followup_notes: We must validate that the moving-average token normalization does not introduce bias for low-volume traffic customers. Schedule A/B validation for 2 weeks after rollout.
Runtime team to provide a compatibility matrix for kernel selection per model architecture and batch-size corner cases by 2025-03-01.
Console team to add visual flags for canaries involving quantized models so on-call cantriage faster.
Consider a 'quiet startup' mode for new quantized shards that initially limit QPS and gradually ramp while maintaining cache warmup stability.
